# Rate and rhythm for the screener

> DRAFT - NOT FOR CLINICAL USE. Contains claims with status 'ai-extracted' that no clinician has verified.

Unit D8 | Tier: Detect | Version 0.1

## You will be able to

- Give the normal fetal heart rate at screening.
- Tell benign ectopic beats from an irregular rhythm that needs assessment.
- Tell transient slowing from persistent bradycardia, and transient speeding from persistent tachycardia.
- Name the rhythm findings that are indications for fetal echocardiography.
- Describe in outline how a specialist works out the mechanism of an arrhythmia.

## Normal

The normal heart rate is 120 to 160 beats per minute, and the rhythm should be regular. [1]

Rate and rhythm are checked on the four-chamber view as part of every screen. The screener's task is not to name the arrhythmia. It is to decide between three answers: normal, watch and re-check, or refer.


## The irregular beat

Ectopic beats, seen as skipped beats, are the most common rhythm disturbance. They are often benign and resolve on their own. In low-risk populations they are not linked to a higher risk of structural heart disease. [2]

Further assessment is indicated when ectopic episodes are frequent, meaning more often than every three to five beats, or when the rhythm stays irregular for more than one to two weeks. [3]


## The slow heart

A brief slow rate, often caused by pressure from the transducer, is seen in normal second-trimester fetuses. [4]

A rate that stays at 110 beats per minute or below in a fetus that is otherwise well needs timely evaluation by a fetal cardiac specialist. Possible causes include frequent blocked atrial ectopic beats, atrioventricular block and sinus bradycardia. [4]

Transducer pressure is a common cause of brief slowing, so ease the pressure and watch the rate. What matters is whether the slow rate persists. [4]


## The fast heart

A mild, brief rise to 160 to 180 beats per minute can be a normal variant during fetal movement. [5]

A rate that stays at 180 beats per minute or above should be evaluated further for a tachyarrhythmia or fetal hypoxia. [5]


## At a glance

Rate and rhythm findings and what each means at screening. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

| Finding | Meaning for the screener |
|---|---|
| 120 to 160 per minute, regular | Normal |
| Occasional skipped beats | Common and often benign |
| Skipped beats more often than every three to five beats, or irregular for more than one to two weeks | Further assessment |
| Brief slowing that recovers, often with probe pressure | Seen in normal fetuses |
| Stays at 110 per minute or below | Timely specialist evaluation |
| Brief rise to 160 to 180 per minute with movement | Can be a normal variant |
| Stays at 180 per minute or above | Further evaluation |


## Rhythm findings that are indications for fetal echocardiography

The guideline lists these among the fetal indications for fetal echocardiography: persistent tachycardia at 180 beats per minute or more, suspected heart block or persistent bradycardia at 110 or less, and a rhythm that is frequently or persistently irregular. [6]


## What the specialist will do

When the rhythm is irregular, slow or fast, the mechanism should be documented with M-mode, pulsed-wave Doppler or tissue Doppler, alone or together. [7]

M-mode times the atria against the ventricles: the cursor passes through an atrial wall and the free wall of a ventricle together. [8]

Pulsed-wave Doppler does the same by sampling two flows at once: superior vena cava with ascending aorta, mitral inflow with aortic outflow, or pulmonary artery with pulmonary vein. [9]

You do not need these techniques to screen. Knowing what they are helps you explain to the family why they are being referred.

## Rate and rhythm at every screen

- [ ] Rate between 120 and 160 per minute [1]
- [ ] Rhythm regular [1]
- [ ] If slow: probe pressure eased and rate watched until it recovers or is shown to persist [4]
- [ ] Persistent rate of 110 or below: specialist evaluation arranged [4]
- [ ] Persistent rate of 180 or above: further evaluation arranged [5]
- [ ] Ectopic beats: frequency noted; re-check arranged; referred if frequent or still irregular after one to two weeks [3]
